paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God keeps His word, even when the story looks like it's just a list of names. Way back, God made promises to Abraham, and here at the end of Abraham's life we see family trees growing everywhere (Gen 25:1-4, 13-16). Abraham's life closes with a man who was "old and contented" (Gen 25:8). I think that's what it looks like to trust God a whole lifetime and finish well.

Now look at who stands at the grave. "His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him" (Gen 25:9). Two sons, with a long and complicated history between them, standing together at one cave. And right after, the text says "God blessed his son Isaac" (Gen 25:11). I think that tells us God's blessing keeps moving forward, even after the faithful one is gone.

The passage also doesn't pretend everything is tidy. Ishmael's descendants "lived in hostility toward all their brothers" (Gen 25:18). Real families are like that, friend, and the Bible tells it straight. So here's what to carry out of my bakery: you don't have to have a perfect family to be part of God's faithful story. Keep trusting Him, and the story isn't over, because more is coming in Isaac's family.
